Post:
From Doug Roberson:
Following the exit from Concacaf Champions Cup, the Galaxy have slowly picked up results and performances. They have shifted from being a very ball-oriented team to a more compact, defensive-structured team that focuses on allowing the front players to try to gain advantages with their quality. They regularly have less than 50% of the ball in games.
Build-up usually starts from central defenders, with a comfort factor with both Jakob Glesnes and Justin Haak or Carlos Emiro Garces trying to start each phase.

Fullbacks are very attack-minded, but the left back can also stay low to build in a back-three system.

Edwin Cerrillo usually anchors the midfield (Haak can also play there ) and is always an option to try to control play. Ahead of him and dependent on where Marco Reus plays, they have dangerous attackers with pace and abilities to take players on.

Both wide players, Joseph Paintsil and Gabriel Pec, will run off the ball behind defenses.

Joao Klaus is key for them if fit because he provides a platform, is an excellent goal-scorer and always has a desire to get in the box.

Reus gets given ball by all the players because he is the cog of the team showing how easy the game looks like with short, simple passes and movements.
They look to spend a lot of time in the mid-block as a default.
Attacking transition: Very dangerous with pace and power. Wide players extremely dangerous breaking quickly and directly, often linking with Klaus and though Reus passing range.

Player Impressions:
Hoyos - does what's expected of him, nothing more
Gregersen - really good charging down a breakaway.  but lets in the breakaways with his positioining.
Berrocal - needs to do better
Báez - good on attack, was beaten badly on defense during breakaways
Muyumba - Plays very well as the DM.  But still outclassed at times.
Sanchez - doing amazing for his age.  Take his age out of it, and he gives the ball away too many times
Galarza - has not been impacting games.  Worried he has triggered his release clause
Miranchuk - played well, but not DP-well.  Has inspiring movement, and passing.  It didn't work tonight.
Saba - his normal.  Great on the run, until he gets to a defender
Latte Lath - played too deep, can't get at the end of plays.  His normal
Fortune - his quality shines through.  He needs to be starting over Galarza
Togashi - has better off the ball movement than Latte Lath.  But can't get at the end of a ball to score
Brennan - At his age and contract situation, he needs to be putting in strong performances.  He isn't.  He will end up being sold or let go.
Santos - Got at the end of a few crosses for a header.  I'm not sure what position he was playing on pitch though.
Mihaj - an upgrade at CB when he came on.

LA were the better team.  Not tactically, not personnel.  They controlled the game state better than Atlanta.
Atlanta were the stronger team in the 1st half, but lost their heads with the Ref.  LA started controlling the game at that point.
In the end, LA were better at managing the game.  They knew how to close out the game and prevent Atlanta from seeing enough of the ball to get a chance.
Atlanta's problems tonight were mental.  Not tactical.
Atlanta received 5 yellow cards.  Will be fined.
